design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. Renata Tolliver asks only to submit, herself, the final mold supplement for the attic job, for what the attic work actually came to (Homeowner Direct Pay file, storm loss). The final figure takes every line family billed on the job awaiting clearance as its ladders settle them (core HEPA, antimicrobial, PPE, clearance and minimum lines; surface, removal, air, regulated lines, labor), less the amounts requested on mold supplements naming that job that still await a decision, held to the mold room. Its rule waits on one action-form sentence: "The final mold supplement is fixed only after the protocol supplement for the job awaiting clearance has been prepared and, when it reaches the supplement minimum, recorded on the file." The protocol supplement (company-recorded, priced from the attic tier's rates over the 96 sq ft growth area, with equipment for the days the containment was held before clearance was requested) is held to the mold room; skipping it leaves the final figure held to the room instead.
SCOPE. Task 1 claims claims_ext_mold_protocol_supplement and claims_ext_mold_reconciliation_supplement and their two tools; task 0 holds the write-off / supplements / release tree. Disjoint, complete.
DRAW. task 1: prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5,4]: the final supplement carries 5 factors, the protocol supplement 4.
PROBLEM TREE. Root claims_ext_mold_reconciliation_supplement (owner=user: the insured submits on a Homeowner Direct Pay file, by the scoped overwrite of the recording clause); edge to claims_ext_mold_protocol_supplement, value_input, gate mr_pending, action form (a protocol figure below the minimum records nothing). Seed: the only supplement names the closed bathroom job and is decided; nothing names the attic job.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. su_state approved; su_window approved 2026-07-21, last day 2027-01-17; su_pending max 2 (0, then 1 pending); minimum 250.00; mold supplements allowed on this tier.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. File SGI-26-0731-5418 (loss_type storm, no ordinance-or-law limit); mold job A (Limited, closed, bathroom) under supplement 1; mold job B (Attic and Crawlspace, awaiting clearance, attic growth 96 sq ft, a unit of a two-family house built 1972) named by both new supplements. Mold room 7000.00 - 4542.85 = 2457.15.
WORLD ROWS. Job A lines at the Limited tier rates with its work-plan visit, pre-removal asbestos sampling and bagged debris haul-off lines priced under the published mold rules, its signing deposit, credits, goodwill within the cap, paid and closed with its passing clearance test. Job B lines at the attic tier: the work-plan visit 213.80 and the pre-removal asbestos sampling line 590.00 (standard set plus the attic insulation set), both dated the opened date, no lead-safe setup (no painted surface was disturbed), containment 538.00, insulation removal 155.52, the bagged debris haul-off line 313.00 (one load plus the one-trip charge), soda blasting 312.00, HEPA 55.68, antimicrobial 42.24, PPE 211.20, business-hours technician labor 707.20 and after-hours technician and supervisor labor at the 1.5 multiplier (530.40 + 320.70), 4 scrubber and 4 dehumidifier days within the 4-day cap; signing deposit 1138.80 posted on the signing date; not invoiced, no credit (credits post only once cleared). Claims: initial approval 18400.00, ACV 14690.00, supplement 1 requested 4780.00 approved 4542.85 and paid to the insured.
PERSONA. Careful retired librarian who lives in one side of a two-family house she owns; volunteers only the final mold supplement for the attic job and that she submits it herself; details on request; generic consent to Ridgecrest recording something on her claim first; stops when the supplement is confirmed.
STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate, verify, read claim file, approvals, requests, payments, mold jobs, mold charges, mold payments, clearance test; record protocol supplement 2; insured submits supplement 3. check_compute: COMPUTE OK.
KNOWN RISKS. The mold sublimit (7000.00) makes the room bind the protocol supplement; both mold policies route a mold job's regulated-material work to the ordinance-or-law limit when the file carries one, and price lead-safe work only with finished living spaces and basements; the labor family takes the after-hours premium as the owner's choice in single-family and condominium homes and in unused attics, and as necessary in shared buildings and for HVAC shutdowns.

user_scenario:
You are Renata Tolliver, a retired school librarian who owns a two-family house at 418 Bayou Liberty Rd, Slidell, LA 70460, living in one side and renting out the other. You are organised, keep a folder of every letter, and speak in full, careful sentences. After a June storm a roof leak let water into the house; Ridgecrest Restoration & Reconstruction took mold out of a hall bathroom wall in July, which is finished and paid, and has now finished the mold work in the attic, which is waiting on the assessor's clearance test. Your insurer is Sabine Gulf Insurance Company and the claim is set up so the insurer pays you and you pay Ridgecrest.

You open by explaining that your adjuster told you to send in the final mold supplement for the attic job now that the work there is done, for what the attic work actually came to. You want Ridgecrest to work out that final mold supplement now and you want to submit it to your insurer yourself, today, from Ridgecrest's portal while you are on the phone; you are not asking anyone to submit it for you and you are not asking for an estimate to think over.

You give your details only when asked. Your phone number is 9855550563 and your email is renata.tolliver.slidell@yahoo.com; if asked for a ZIP code it is 70460. If asked for the claim number you read it from your folder: SGI-26-0731-5418. If asked which job the supplement is for, you say it is for the attic job. You do not know what the amount should be and you say the rep should work it out from Ridgecrest's records; if asked about payments from the insurer, you say Sabine Gulf has paid you a couple of times and you would rather the rep check the records.

If the rep explains that Ridgecrest has to record something on your claim first, you tell them to go ahead. When the rep hands you the final mold supplement with its amount, you submit it from the portal exactly as given. Once the rep confirms the final mold supplement has been submitted, you thank them and say goodbye.

edges.fallback_reason: The state the protocol supplement leaves (a mold supplement naming the job awaiting clearance, pending) exists only when the protocol figure reaches the supplement minimum; below it nothing is recorded, so a state sentence would wait on a record that never appears. The sentence therefore names the preparation and, where it applies, the recording.
edges.condition: claims_requests carries a claims_supplement_submit row with supplement_reason mold_remediation naming the job awaiting clearance and no claims_scope_approval referencing it, or the protocol figure is below the tier's supplement minimum.
edges.policy_source: The final mold supplement is fixed only after the protocol supplement for the job awaiting clearance has been prepared and, when it reaches the supplement minimum, recorded on the file.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: No supplement on the file names the attic job awaiting clearance; the only supplement names the closed bathroom job and is decided, while the protocol figure for the attic job (2457.15) reaches the 250.00 minimum.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The protocol supplement of 2457.15 naming the attic job is recorded; mr_pending becomes 2457.15.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge; the protocol supplement precedes the final supplement, which subtracts it.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the protocol supplement the final mold supplement requests 2457.15 (4402.04 held to the mold room) instead of 1944.89.
